guide.summary: Temples, shrines, museums, observation decks and gardens, plus breakfast cafés, noodle lunches, dinners and cocktail bars, each checked against its own or its public operator's website.
guide.tip: Watch the closing days: the Tokyo National Museum closes on Mondays, the Imperial Palace East Gardens on Mondays and Fridays, and Bar High Five on Sundays and national holidays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Tokyo National Museum and Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden close on Mondays (the next weekday if Monday is a holiday). The Imperial Palace East Gardens close every Monday and Friday.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Narisawa takes reservations only through its online booking site, not by phone. The Tokyo National Museum recommends buying tickets online because waits at its security screening can exceed 30 minutes.

toolkit.label: Walk-in policies
toolkit.copy: Bar High Five has taken no reservations since May 2015 and admits its last guests at 00:00, Monday to Saturday. At Udon Shin noodles are made to order, so expect a 10 to 15 minute wait after you order.

toolkit.label: Bags and rules
toolkit.copy: The Tokyo National Museum does not allow suitcases and screens visitors at the Main Gate. AFURI (Ebisu) is marked fully cashless, so bring a card.

guide.dek: Do the early-closing sights first: Senso-ji's main hall shuts at 5pm and Meiji Jingu's gates close in late afternoon, while observation decks and bars run late.
intro: You can start early at Senso-ji in Asakusa: from October to March its main hall opens at 6:30 a.m. and closes at 5:00 p.m. Meiji Jingu's gate hours follow the sun, 5:40 a.m. to 4:40 p.m. in October and 6:10 a.m. to 4:10 p.m. in November, so a morning visit leaves time for more. The Imperial Palace East Gardens are free, but they close every Monday and Friday, and from November the last entry is 3:30 p.m.

In Ueno, the Tokyo National Museum is showing the special exhibition Hiroshige: New Perspectives on Edo Japan from September 29 to December 20, 2026. It opens 9:30 to 17:00 and is closed on Mondays. Admission to the collection is free if you are under 18 or over 70. Suitcases are not allowed, and the museum suggests buying tickets online because queues at its security screening can run past 30 minutes. Next door, Ueno Zoo has posted partial path closures from October 26 to November 16.

For views, Tokyo Skytree lists hours of 10:00 to 22:00 with final entry at 21:00, and its Dream Christmas event runs November 5 to December 25. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building's observation decks are free: the south deck admits visitors until 21:30 but closes on the first and third Tuesdays of the month. In Roppongi, the Mori Art Museum reopens on October 31 with Mariko Mori: All That Shines, which runs to March 28, 2027. Tokyo City View, one floor below, is closed October 27 and November 10 to 12.

For food, Ivy Place in Daikanyama serves breakfast from 8:00, and Fuglen Tokyo in Tomigaya opens at 7am. At lunch you can choose AFURI (Ebisu), which is cashless, or Udon Shin in Yoyogi, where every bowl is cut and boiled to order. Gonpachi (Nishi-Azabu) is open daily until 27:30, and Narisawa accepts bookings online only. To end the night, Bar High Five in Ginza is open Monday to Saturday from 17:00 and does not take reservations.
summaryCards: Pair Senso-ji's early main-hall opening with the Tokyo National Museum's Hiroshige exhibition, which runs to December 20, 2026, remembering the museum closes on Mondays.
Have breakfast at Ivy Place from 8:00 or Fuglen Tokyo (Tomigaya) from 7am, then walk to Meiji Jingu before its gates close in the late afternoon.
Book Narisawa through its online reservation site, because it takes no phone bookings, and note that Bar High Five takes no reservations at all.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several sites could not be read: SHIBUYA SKY and teamLab Planets returned only empty script shells, Bills returned no content, and Sushi Daiwa, Bar Benfiddich, Path and 365 Days failed DNS lookups. fuglen.com had an expired certificate, which was not bypassed. None of these failures is evidence of closure. Tsukiji Outer Market was left out only because its official pages give no postal address. Some places were published only partially: Ueno Zoo's visitor hours page did not load, Shinjuku Gyoen's hours and Narisawa's and The SG Club's hours were not published, and Narisawa's address appears only in a map link. Udon Shin, Glitch Coffee, AFURI, Fuglen Tokyo, Ivy Place and the Imperial Palace East Gardens are supported by currently published hours or booking links rather than 2026-dated content. Tokyo Skytree's stated hours were shown as 'today's' hours without a date. Fewer than 25 places were confirmed, because many input entries were generic or unreadable and the gap-candidate limit of 8 was reached.
